A rare opportunity

Geoff Lawton is one of permaculture’s most recognised teachers and practitioners. He completed his Permaculture Design Certificate with co-founder Bill Mollison in 1983, later taught alongside him, and in 1997 was asked by Mollison to establish and direct the Permaculture Research Institute on Tagari Farm. After more than four decades of practice, design and teaching around the world, Geoff is now stepping back from travel and teaching. That makes this gathering in Portugal an unusually rare chance to learn with him in the field.

The field experience

Learn to read the land before you design it.

Monte Ventosa offers 140 hectares of real Mediterranean land — a place where water, access, vegetation, microclimates and future infrastructure can be read together in context.

The course is being developed with Geoff Lawton and his team. Rather than presenting a finished curriculum before it is confirmed, the page will be updated with the final programme as soon as the details are agreed.

The current direction includes landscape reading, water movement, contours and catchments, access, existing vegetation, microclimates, mapping and placement decisions.

A rare moment

At the very beginning — when the questions are still open and the landscape can still be listened to.

The event is expected to be part of what may be Geoff Lawton’s final European tour. Final wording will be updated once the tour details are formally confirmed.

What you may take away

See patterns. Read relationships. Make better decisions.

The deepest value may not be a list of techniques. It may be learning how to notice the relationships that shape every good decision on land.

Landscape literacyRead patterns, terrain, vegetation and context with greater confidence.
Water thinkingUnderstand how water movement influences the whole system.
Decision makingLearn to delay intervention until the landscape has been understood.
ConnectionMeet people who care about regenerative land, permaculture and practical change.
Learn from experience

More than four decades of permaculture practice and teaching.

The place

Meet Monte Ventosa.

Open land, water, cork oaks, wild Mediterranean vegetation and existing farm structures — with enough space to observe before deciding what belongs where.

Stay close to the land

Wake up where the learning happens.

This is not a hotel-based course. The invitation is to spend these days immersed in the landscape itself.

You can arrive in your own campervan or bring a tent. Monte Ventosa also has plenty of trees and beautiful places for hammocks and hammock tents. We are exploring partnerships that may allow us to provide a limited number of tents, hammocks or hammock tents for participants who cannot bring their own.

If you prefer a bed and four walls, we can also share information about nearby guesthouses and Airbnb-style accommodation in the participant handout.

Food & shared tables

Come to learn. We’ll take care of the meals.

Breakfast, lunch and dinner are planned, together with tea and coffee breaks and small snacks throughout the day.

Vegetarian and vegan options will be available. Final meal format will be confirmed before registration opens, and dietary preferences, allergies and intolerances will be collected during registration so the kitchen team can plan properly.

Who this may be for

For people who want to understand land, not simply copy a formula.

Land stewards

People responsible for land who want to make better long-term decisions.

Permaculture practitioners

Learners and teachers who want to deepen landscape-reading skills in a real Mediterranean context.

People at a beginning

Those planning farms, homesteads, regenerative projects or new relationships with land.

Volunteer / Work Exchange

Join the build-up — and help the place keep flowing

Volunteer roles may include preparing temporary infrastructure, helping with the olive harvest, supporting the kitchen, keeping showers and toilets clean and usable, creating activities and small projects with children, watering the garden, caring for animals and helping everyday life at Monte Ventosa continue smoothly while the course is running.

A dedicated Volunteer / Work Exchange page will follow with roles, timing and practical details.

For companies

Put useful solutions into real use

Selected partners can place products, infrastructure, expertise or funding into a real-world regenerative setting — gaining authentic visibility, practical use and the possibility of becoming part of a longer-term collaboration.

A dedicated Partnerships & Collaborations page will follow.

The wider story

Part of Terra-Be-Utopia

Monte Ventosa is connected to a broader initiative exploring regenerative demonstration projects, learning and new relationships between people and place.
